text:
HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE
Use this cover for the formal client UAT session. Confirm the project name, client, date, tested version, and presenter.

SUGGESTED CLIENT-FACING WORDING
Good [morning/afternoon]. Today we will review the project progress, validate the agreed solution, record the results, and confirm the next step.

name: Rectangle 5
text: The presentation covers project progress before moving into client validation and approval.

text: Keep the project story short enough to leave most of the session for client testing and decisions.
textPreview: Keep the project story short enough to leave most of the session for client testing and decisions.

text:
HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE
Use this slide as the agenda. State that the client will see the complete project status before testing begins.

SUGGESTED CLIENT-FACING WORDING
We will first confirm what the project set out to deliver and where it stands. We will then complete the UAT cycle and agree on the decision and follow-up actions.

name: Rectangle 5
text: Summarize the business reason for the project before discussing features or technical details.

text:
HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE
Use plain business language. Do not begin with technical architecture unless the client asks for it.

SUGGESTED CLIENT-FACING WORDING
This project started because [business problem]. The agreed objective was [objective]. Today we will validate whether the completed solution supports that objective.

name: Rectangle 5
text: Set the testing boundary before showing progress or accepting new requests.

text:

Confirm the baseline that UAT will validate. If the client disputes the scope, stop and reconcile the approved records.

SUGGESTED CLIENT-FACING WORDING
These are the items included in the approved project and the measures we will use during acceptance. New ideas will be recorded for assessment after the session.

name: Rectangle 5
text: Show the client how the project moved from approval to UAT.

text: Use actual approval and completion dates. Do not present estimated work as completed work.

text:
HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE
Replace each date and output. Highlight the current UAT stage and the planned handover gate.

SUGGESTED CLIENT-FACING WORDING
The project completed the approved discovery, design, build, and internal testing activities. We are now at UAT, where your users validate the solution before final handover.

name: Rectangle 5
text: Present completion by deliverable, supported by evidence rather than a general percentage alone.
textPreview: Present completion by deliverable, supported by evidence rather than a general percentage alone.

text:
HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE
Populate using the project tracker and approved deliverables. Explain any incomplete or deferred item and its effect on UAT.

SUGGESTED CLIENT-FACING WORDING
The project is [percentage] complete based on the approved deliverables. These items are ready for UAT, while [item] remains [status] because [reason].

text: Connect completed features to the client’s daily work.

text:
HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE
Use one row for each important business capability. Avoid listing technical tasks that the client cannot validate.

SUGGESTED CLIENT-FACING WORDING
The completed solution supports these business areas. Each capability connects to a UAT scenario that your users will perform today.

name: Rectangle 5
text: Show how approved changes affected the final scope, schedule, or solution.

text:
HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE
Include only approved changes and decisions relevant to the final solution or UAT. Keep unapproved requests in the issue and action log.

SUGGESTED CLIENT-FACING WORDING
These approved changes explain how the final solution differs from the original plan. The UAT scope already reflects these decisions.

text: Clarify what the client is validating and the decision expected at the end of the cycle.

text:
HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE
Use this transition slide before readiness and testing. Make the expected decision explicit.

SUGGESTED CLIENT-FACING WORDING
UAT allows your authorized users to confirm that the agreed solution works for the approved business processes. At the end, we will record the acceptance status and any remaining actions.

name: Rectangle 5
text: Confirm that the system, people, data, and documents are ready before client testing begins.

text:
HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE
Update the status immediately before the meeting. If an item is not ready, state its effect and the revised testing plan.

SUGGESTED CLIENT-FACING WORDING
Before testing begins, we will confirm each readiness item. Any critical gap will be resolved or the affected scenario will be rescheduled.

name: Rectangle 5
text: Confirm who will test, what access they have, and what data supports the scenarios.

text:
HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE
Use totals and sample records to show that the correct data was loaded. Do not expose passwords or unnecessary sensitive information.

SUGGESTED CLIENT-FACING WORDING
We prepared the users and test data based on the approved records. Please confirm the roles, source file, counts, and important totals before we execute the scenarios.

text:
HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE
Display this slide before the first test case. Repeat the method when new testers join.

SUGGESTED CLIENT-FACING WORDING
For every scenario, we will state the task, let the assigned user perform it, compare the result, save appropriate evidence, and record the status together.

text:

Populate the counts and important scenario results after testing. Do not label an unexecuted scenario as passed.

SUGGESTED CLIENT-FACING WORDING
We completed [number] scenarios. [Number] passed, while the remaining items require the actions shown in the next slide.

name: Rectangle 5
text: Separate confirmed defects from data, access, training, and new-scope concerns.

text:
HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE
Review each open item with the client. State whether it affects acceptance. Escalate material commitments for CEO approval before confirming them.

SUGGESTED CLIENT-FACING WORDING
We classified each concern so the right action is clear. These are the owners, target dates, and retesting requirements agreed during the session.

name: Rectangle 5
text: Record one decision supported by the completed tests, evidence, and agreed actions.
textPreview: Record one decision supported by the completed tests, evidence, and agreed actions.

Select only the applicable status in the final client copy. Link the signed or written approval record after the meeting.

Based on the completed tests and recorded evidence, the proposed UAT status is [status]. Please confirm the reason, conditions, and authorized approval record.

text: Close the UAT cycle with owners, dates, and the next decision gate.

HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE
Confirm every owner and target date before ending. Send the written record promptly and prepare the separate final handover presentation after UAT approval.

To close today’s UAT cycle, these are the agreed next steps, owners, and dates. I will send the written record for confirmation and prepare the final handover once the acceptance requirements are complete.
